subproblem.title: Converging normal averages force positive mass on every ball
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and y, v ∈ ℝ^P with v ≠ 0. Let A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ, where μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal, 0^{-1} = 0 and the integral is the Bochner integral. Suppose A(ρ) → v as ρ → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0). Then μ(B̄_r(y)) ≠ 0 for every r > 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P → Euclid P) (y v : Euclid P), v ≠ 0 → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (μ (closedBall y ρ)).toReal⁻¹ • ∫ z in closedBall y ρ, ν z ∂μ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 v) → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → μ (closedBall y r) ≠ 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 ('Since ⟨A(r), v⟩ → 1, A(r) ≠ 0 for small r, so μ(B̄_r) > 0 for small r and, by monotonicity, for every r > 0'). Only v ≠ 0 is needed.
1. A(ρ) → v as ρ → 0⁺ and v ≠ 0. Since ℝ^P ∖ {0} is an open neighbourhood of v, A(ρ) ≠ 0 eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_ne).
2. Fix r > 0. The interval (0, r) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). The filter 𝓝[>] 0 is proper, so the intersection of the two eventual sets is nonempty: there is ρ with 0 < ρ < r and A(ρ) ≠ 0.
3. Suppose μ(B̄_r(y)) = 0. Since B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B̄_r(y), also μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = 0. Then μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ = 0, its inverse is 0 (convention 0^{-1} = 0), and A(ρ) = 0 • ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ = 0, contradicting step 2. Hence μ(B̄_r(y)) ≠ 0. ∎
Validation note (not part of the proof): a Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement compiled against the frozen import closure with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (scratch file /tmp/vdl-split-check/G/Proof.lean, outside the repository).
proof_key_steps: A(ρ) → v ≠ 0 implies A(ρ) ≠ 0 eventually as ρ ↓ 0.
μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = 0 would force A(ρ) = 0; monotonicity then gives μ(B̄_r(y)) ≠ 0.

audit.reason: The generality of the prose matches the exact type. Convergence to a nonzero vector gives eventual nonzero averages; properness of the right-neighbourhood filter supplies a smaller positive radius. A zero mass on the larger ball would force zero mass and hence a zero average there. No measurability, integrability or finiteness assumption is silently required.
